review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

7:1.sourceText: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεύς Εἰ ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει;
7:1.targetText: Then the high priest asked Stephen, “Are these charges true?”

groups.note: ταῦτα ("these things") is rendered these charges.
οὕτως ("so", in οὕτως ἔχει "are [they] so") is rendered true.

unmappedSource.reason: Here εἰ introduces a direct question and has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the one asked; the Greek has no addressee.

7:2.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἔφη Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατε. Ὁ Θεὸς τῆς δόξης ὤφθη τῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν Ἀβραὰμ ὄντι ἐν τῇ Μεσοποταμίᾳ πρὶν ἢ κατοικῆσαι αὐτὸν ἐν Χαρράν,
7:2.targetText: And Stephen declared: “Brothers and fathers, listen to me! The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,

groups.note: The article ὁ, used as a pronoun ("he"), is rendered by the name Stephen.
Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ("men, brothers") is rendered Brothers.
The participle ὄντι ("being") is rendered while he was.
πρὶν ἤ ("before") is rendered before.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for listen; ἀκούσατε has none.
English adds still; the participle ὄντι has no adverb.

7:3.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ τῆς συγγενείας σου, καὶ δεῦρο εἰς τὴν γῆν ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω.
7:3.targetText: and told him, ‘Leave your country and your kindred and go to the land I will show you.’

unmappedSource.reason: The preposition πρός ("to") is absorbed into the English told him.
The preposition ἐκ ("out of") is absorbed into the English verb Leave.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The relative ἣν ἄν ("whichever") is left implicit in the English the land I will show you.

7:4.sourceText: τότε ἐξελθὼν ἐκ γῆς Χαλδαίων κατῴκησεν ἐν Χαρράν. κἀκεῖθεν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ μετῴκισεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν γῆν ταύτην εἰς ἣν ὑμεῖς νῦν κατοικεῖτε,
7:4.targetText: So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. After his father died, God brought him out of that place and into this land where you are now living.

groups.note: κἀκεῖθεν ("and from there") is rendered out of that place.
The articular infinitive τὸ ἀποθανεῖν ("the dying") is rendered died.
εἰς ἥν ("into which") is rendered where.

unmappedSource.reason: The preposition ἐκ ("out of") is absorbed into the English verb left.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives him only in the participle ἐξελθών.
English joins the participle ἐξελθών, rendered left, to the main verb settled.
English names the subject; the Greek gives Him only in the verb ending of μετῴκισεν.
English joins out of that place and into this land; the καί of κἀκεῖθεν joins the clauses.

7:5.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κληρονομίαν ἐν αὐτῇ οὐδὲ βῆμα ποδός, καὶ ἐπηγγείλατο δοῦναι αὐτῷ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτόν, οὐκ ὄντος αὐτῷ τέκνου.
7:5.targetText: He gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground. But God promised to give possession of the land to Abraham and his descendants, even though he did not yet have a child.

groups.note: ἐν αὐτῇ ("in it", the land) is rendered here.
βῆμα ποδός ("the step of a foot") is rendered a foot of ground.
The pronoun αὐτῷ ("to him") is rendered by the name Abraham.
εἰς κατάσχεσιν ("as a possession") is rendered possession, the object of give.
The pronoun αὐτήν ("it", the land) is rendered of the land.
The genitive absolute οὐκ ὄντος αὐτῷ τέκνου ("there being no child to him") is rendered even though he did not have a child.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence; the opening καί is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves μετ’ αὐτόν ("after him") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives Him only in the verb ending of ἐπηγγείλατο.
English adds yet; the Greek has no adverb.

7:6.sourceText: ἐλάλησεν δὲ οὕτως ὁ Θεὸς, ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ πάροικον ἐν γῇ ἀλλοτρίᾳ, καὶ δουλώσουσιν αὐτὸ καὶ κακώσουσιν ἔτη τετρακόσια·
7:6.targetText: God told him that his descendants would be foreigners in a strange land, and that they would be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.

groups.note: ὅτι governs both clauses; BSB repeats that before the second.
The active δουλώσουσιν αὐτό ("they will enslave it") is rendered as a passive.
The object αὐτό ("it", the descendants) becomes the subject they of the English passive.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves οὕτως ("thus") untranslated; that introduces what God said.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the person addressed; ἐλάλησεν has no object.

7:7.sourceText: καὶ τὸ ἔθνος ᾧ ἐὰν δουλεύσουσιν κρινῶ ἐγώ, ὁ Θεὸς εἶπεν, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξελεύσονται καὶ λατρεύσουσίν μοι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τούτῳ.
7:7.targetText: ‘But I will punish the nation that enslaves them,’ God said, ‘and afterward they will come forth and worship Me in this place.’

groups.note: The relative clause "to which they will be slaves" is recast: ᾧ becomes that and the verb's subject becomes them.
μετὰ ταῦτα ("after these things") is rendered afterward.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle ἐάν (here = ἄν, "whatever") has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:8.sourceText: καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ διαθήκην περιτομῆς· καὶ οὕτως ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ, καὶ Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακώβ, καὶ Ἰακὼβ τοὺς δώδεκα πατριάρχας.
7:8.targetText: Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. And Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτῷ ("to him") is rendered by the name Abraham.
ἐγέννησεν ("fathered") is understood again with Isaac and with Jacob, where BSB repeats became the father of.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὕτως ("so", "in this way") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives Him only in the verb ending of ἔδωκεν.
English names the subject; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending of ἐγέννησεν.

7:9.sourceText: Καὶ οἱ πατριάρχαι ζηλώσαντες τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀπέδοντο εἰς Αἴγυπτον· καὶ ἦν ὁ Θεὸς μετ’ αὐτοῦ,
7:9.targetText: Because the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph, they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him

groups.note: The participle ζηλώσαντες ("being jealous") is rendered Because … were jealous.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; the Greek names Joseph once, as the object of ζηλώσαντες.
English adds as a slave; ἀπέδοντο means only "sold".

7:10.sourceText: καὶ ἐξείλατο αὐτὸν ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ χάριν καὶ σοφίαν ἐναντίον Φαραὼ βασιλέως Αἰγύπτου, καὶ κατέστησεν αὐτὸν ἡγούμενον ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον καὶ ὅλον τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
7:10.targetText: and rescued him from all his troubles. He granted Joseph favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt, who appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his household.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτῷ ("to him") is rendered by the name Joseph.
BSB turns the clause into a relative clause; who stands for the subject of κατέστησεν (Pharaoh).

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here; the καί is not separately expressed.
BSB turns the καί clause into a relative clause with who, so καί has no English word.

7:11.sourceText: ἦλθεν δὲ λιμὸς ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν Αἴγυπτον καὶ Χανάαν καὶ θλῖψις μεγάλη, καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον χορτάσματα οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν.
7:11.targetText: Then famine and great suffering swept across Egypt and Canaan, and our fathers could not find food.

groups.note: ἐφ’ ὅλην ("over all of") is rendered across.
The imperfect ηὕρισκον ("were finding") is rendered could … find.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:12.sourceText: ἀκούσας δὲ Ἰακὼβ ὄντα σιτία εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἐξαπέστειλεν τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν πρῶτον·
7:12.targetText: When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers on their first visit.

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσας ("having heard") is rendered When … heard.
The adverb πρῶτον ("first", "the first time") is rendered on their first visit.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies that before the reported fact; the Greek uses the participle ὄντα.

7:13.sourceText: καὶ ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ ἐγνωρίσθη Ἰωσὴφ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ, καὶ φανερὸν ἐγένετο τῷ Φαραὼ τὸ γένος Ἰωσήφ.
7:13.targetText: On their second visit, Joseph revealed his identity to his brothers, and his family became known to Pharaoh.

groups.note: The article τῷ is rendered their (their second visit).
The passive ἐγνωρίσθη ("was made known") is rendered revealed his identity; BSB's Greek has a different word here with the same meaning.
The name Ἰωσήφ ("of Joseph") is rendered his.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:14.sourceText: ἀποστείλας δὲ Ἰωσὴφ μετεκαλέσατο Ἰακὼβ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν συγγένειαν ἐν ψυχαῖς ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε.
7:14.targetText: Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five in all.

groups.note: ἀποστείλας … μετεκαλέσατο ("having sent, he summoned") is rendered sent for.
The article τήν is used as a possessive and rendered his.
ἐν ψυχαῖς ("in souls", i.e. persons) is rendered in all.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:15.sourceText: καὶ κατέβη Ἰακὼβ εἰς Αἴγυπτον, καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν,
7:15.targetText: So Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our fathers died.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB joins the clauses with where instead of and, so this καί has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English links the clause to Egypt with where; the Greek has καί ("and").

7:16.sourceText: καὶ μετετέθησαν εἰς Συχὲμ καὶ ἐτέθησαν ἐν τῷ μνήματι ᾧ ὠνήσατο Ἀβραὰμ τιμῆς ἀργυρίου παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἐμμὼρ ἐν Συχέμ.
7:16.targetText: Their bones were carried back to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor at Shechem for a price he paid in silver.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject; μετετέθησαν ("they were moved") has no noun for bones.
English adds he paid; the Greek has the genitive of price only.

7:17.sourceText: Καθὼς δὲ ἤγγιζεν ὁ χρόνος τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἧς ὡμολόγησεν ὁ Θεὸς τῷ Ἀβραάμ, ηὔξησεν ὁ λαὸς καὶ ἐπληθύνθη ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ,
7:17.targetText: As the time drew near for God to fulfill His promise to Abraham, our people in Egypt increased greatly in number.

groups.note: The article τῆς is rendered His (God's promise).
The article ὁ is used as a possessive and rendered our.
ἐπληθύνθη ("multiplied") is rendered greatly in number, added to increased.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB recasts the relative clause ἧς ὡμολόγησεν ("which [God] had declared") as His promise to Abraham, without a verb for declared.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB merges the two verbs into increased greatly in number, so καί has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English expands "the time of the promise" into the time for God to fulfill His promise.
English expands "the time of the promise" into the time for God to fulfill His promise.

7:18.sourceText: ἄχρι οὗ ἀνέστη βασιλεὺς ἕτερος ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον, ὃς οὐκ ᾔδει τὸν Ἰωσήφ.
7:18.targetText: Then another king, who knew nothing of Joseph, arose over Egypt.

groups.note: ἄχρι οὗ ("until") is rendered Then, beginning a new sentence.
οὐκ ᾔδει ("did not know") is rendered knew nothing.

7:19.sourceText: οὗτος κατασοφισάμενος τὸ γένος ἡμῶν ἐκάκωσεν τοὺς πατέρας τοῦ ποιεῖν τὰ βρέφη ἔκθετα αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ μὴ ζωογονεῖσθαι.
7:19.targetText: He exploited our people and oppressed our fathers, forcing them to abandon their infants so they would die.

groups.note: The articular infinitive τοῦ ποιεῖν ("so as to make") is rendered forcing.
ἔκθετα ("exposed", "cast out") is rendered to abandon.
εἰς τό with the infinitive ("so that") is rendered so.
μὴ ζωογονεῖσθαι ("not be kept alive") is rendered they would die.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle κατασοφισάμενος, rendered exploited, to the main verb oppressed.
BSB follows a reading with an extra word here (our fathers), which N1904 lacks.
English supplies the object of forcing; the Greek has none.

7:20.sourceText: Ἐν ᾧ καιρῷ ἐγεννήθη Μωϋσῆς, καὶ ἦν ἀστεῖος τῷ Θεῷ· ὃς ἀνετράφη μῆνας τρεῖς ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ πατρός·
7:20.targetText: At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful in the sight of God. For three months he was nurtured in his father’s house.

groups.note: The dative τῷ Θεῷ ("to God") is rendered in the sight of God.
The accusative μῆνας gives the length of time, rendered For.
The article τοῦ is used as a possessive and rendered his.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:21.sourceText: ἐκτεθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀνείλατο αὐτὸν ἡ θυγάτηρ Φαραὼ καὶ ἀνεθρέψατο αὐτὸν ἑαυτῇ εἰς υἱόν.
7:21.targetText: When he was set outside, Pharaoh’s daughter took him and brought him up as her own son.

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἐκτεθέντος αὐτοῦ ("when he had been put out") is rendered When he was set outside.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:22.sourceText: καὶ ἐπαιδεύθη Μωϋσῆς πάσῃ σοφίᾳ Αἰγυπτίων, ἦν δὲ δυνατὸς ἐν λόγοις καὶ ἔργοις αὐτοῦ.
7:22.targetText: So Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was powerful in speech and action.

groups.note: The dative σοφίᾳ is rendered in … wisdom; BSB's Greek has an extra word here with the same meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB's in speech and action leaves αὐτοῦ ("his") without an English word.

7:23.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦτο αὐτῷ τεσσερακονταέτης χρόνος, ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ ἐπισκέψασθαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ.
7:23.targetText: When Moses was forty years old, he decided to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

groups.note: ἐπληροῦτο … χρόνος ("the time was being completed") is rendered was … old.
The pronoun αὐτῷ ("for him") is rendered by the name Moses.
ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ ("it came up into his heart") is rendered he decided.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:24.sourceText: καὶ ἰδών τινα ἀδικούμενον ἠμύνατο, καὶ ἐποίησεν ἐκδίκησιν τῷ καταπονουμένῳ πατάξας τὸν Αἰγύπτιον.
7:24.targetText: And when he saw one of them being mistreated, Moses went to his defense and avenged him by striking down the Egyptian who was oppressing him.

groups.note: The indefinite τινα ("someone") is rendered one of them.
ἐποίησεν ἐκδίκησιν ("did justice") is rendered avenged.
τῷ καταπονουμένῳ ("for the one being oppressed") is rendered him … who was oppressing him, with the passive turned active.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending of ἠμύνατο.

7:25.sourceText: ἐνόμιζεν δὲ συνιέναι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς διὰ χειρὸς αὐτοῦ δίδωσιν σωτηρίαν αὐτοῖς· οἱ δὲ οὐ συνῆκαν.
7:25.targetText: He assumed his brothers would understand that God was using him to deliver them, but they did not.

groups.note: διὰ χειρός ("by the hand of") is rendered was using.
δίδωσιν σωτηρίαν ("is giving salvation") is rendered to deliver.
The article οἱ, used as a pronoun, is rendered they.
συνῆκαν ("understood") is rendered by did, standing for understand.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here (his brothers), which N1904 lacks.

7:26.sourceText: τῇ τε ἐπιούσῃ ἡμέρᾳ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς μαχομένοις, καὶ συνήλλασσεν αὐτοὺς εἰς εἰρήνην εἰπών Ἄνδρες, ἀδελφοί ἐστε· ἵνα τί ἀδικεῖτε ἀλλήλους;
7:26.targetText: The next day he came upon two Israelites who were fighting, and he tried to reconcile them, saying, ‘Men, you are brothers. Why are you mistreating each other?’

groups.note: ὤφθη ("he appeared") is rendered he came upon.
The pronoun αὐτοῖς ("to them") is rendered Israelites.
συνήλλασσεν … εἰς εἰρήνην ("tried to bring them into peace") is rendered tried to reconcile.
ἵνα τί ("for what purpose") is rendered Why.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective τε is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the number; the Greek has only αὐτοῖς ("them").

7:27.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀδικῶν τὸν πλησίον ἀπώσατο αὐτὸν εἰπών Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστὴν ἐφ’ ἡμῶν;
7:27.targetText: But the man who was abusing his neighbor pushed Moses aside and said, ‘Who made you ruler and judge over us?

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the one wronging", is rendered the man who was abusing.
The article τόν is used as a possessive and rendered his.
The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name Moses.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle εἰπών, rendered said, to the main verb pushed aside.

7:28.sourceText: μὴ ἀνελεῖν με σὺ θέλεις ὃν τρόπον ἀνεῖλες ἐχθὲς τὸν Αἰγύπτιον;
7:28.targetText: Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’

groups.note: ὃν τρόπον ("in the way that") is rendered as.

unmappedSource.reason: Here μή introduces a question expecting the answer no and has no English word.

7:29.sourceText: ἔφυγεν δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ, καὶ ἐγένετο πάροικος ἐν γῇ Μαδιάμ, οὗ ἐγέννησεν υἱοὺς δύο.

7:30.sourceText: Καὶ πληρωθέντων ἐτῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὤφθη αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τοῦ ὄρους Σινᾶ ἄγγελος ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς βάτου.

7:31.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἰδὼν ἐθαύμαζεν τὸ ὅραμα· προσερχομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ κατανοῆσαι ἐγένετο φωνὴ Κυρίου

7:32.sourceText: Ἐγὼ ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου, ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακώβ. ἔντρομος δὲ γενόμενος Μωϋσῆς οὐκ ἐτόλμα κατανοῆσαι.

7:33.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Κύριος Λῦσον τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν σου· ὁ γὰρ τόπος ἐφ’ ᾧ ἕστηκας γῆ ἁγία ἐστίν.
